author: sjm41
body:
**UniProt UniRule (ID and label):**
RU000393

**Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
E1JH26 (Dmel Ccs) 

**Description of issue**
E1JH26 (Dmel) and its ortholog O14618 (human) represent the CCS protein, which is characterized as a 'Copper chaperone for superoxide dismutase' - ie. it doesn't itself have catalytic activity.

However, E1JH26 (Dmel) gets the following catalytic annotations:
- Rhea 20696/EC:1.15.1.1 via ARBA: ARBA00049204 / UniRule RuleBase: RU000393
- Keyword 'oxidoreductase' via ARBA: ARBA00023002 / UniRule RuleBase: RU000393

Can those ARBA/UniRules be reviewed so that the catalytic terms are not applied to this chaperone protein?

Thanks.
title: Incorrect Unirule mapping: RU000393

author: Antonialock
body:
I think there are two things going on.

For unirule, it excludes proteins with [PF00403](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro/entry/pfam/PF00403)  - this pfam seems to be present in other swiss-prot ccs proteins, except dicty Q54F73 and it is also absent from drosophila

For ARBA, we have 22 SP entries with the combination of  [IPR001424 + IPR024134 + taxon 33392](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb?query=%28xref%3Ainterpro-IPR001424%29+AND+%28xref%3Ainterpro-IPR024134%29+AND+%28taxonomy_id%3A33392%29&facets=reviewed%3Atrue). These are all superoxide dismutases.

I can manually curate the fly CCS protein, and this domain + taxon combination should be removed from the rule, but I'm a bit concerned about the logic here....it's like this annotation is allowed in insects because we had (by chance) enough superoxide dismutases annotated to generate the rule in insects...there will be other taxon groups where we have a lot of SP entries for one ortholog protein (historically I think entries were integrated into SP differently, today we only integrate if there are papers for an entry, but it doesn't seem to have always been the case for flies or fungi for some reason).
